title: Maps on cohomology of modules induced by f-maps (pullback, edge map)
statement: Let $h:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], $\mathcal G$ an $\mathcal O_Y$-module, $\mathcal F$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module and $\varphi:\mathcal G\to h_*\mathcal F$ a morphism of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules (an *$h$-map* from $\mathcal G$ to $\mathcal F$; equivalently, by the adjunction $h^*\dashv h_*$ [def-pc-module-pullback], a morphism $h^*\mathcal G\to\mathcal F$). For $p\ge0$ the map $\varphi^*:H^p(Y,\mathcal G)\to H^p(X,\mathcal F)$ [pqf-def-cohomology] is defined as follows: choose an injective resolution $\mathcal F\to\mathcal I^\bullet$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules, an injective resolution $\mathcal G\to\mathcal J^\bullet$ and a resolution $h_*\mathcal I^\bullet\to\mathcal J'^\bullet$ by a complex of injective $\mathcal O_Y$-modules, and a morphism of complexes $\beta:\mathcal J^\bullet\to\mathcal J'^\bullet$ compatible with $\mathcal G\to h_*\mathcal F\to h_*\mathcal I^\bullet\to\mathcal J'^\bullet$ (it exists and is unique up to homotopy); the map $\Gamma(Y,h_*\mathcal I^\bullet)=\Gamma(X,\mathcal I^\bullet)\to\Gamma(Y,\mathcal J'^\bullet)$ is a quasi-isomorphism, and $\varphi^*$ is $H^p$ of $\Gamma(Y,\beta)$ followed by the inverse of $H^p$ of this quasi-isomorphism. It is $\mathcal O_Y(Y)$-linear, $\mathcal O_Y(Y)$ acting on $H^p(X,\mathcal F)$ through $h^\sharp:\mathcal O_Y(Y)\to\mathcal O_X(X)$, and in degree $0$ it is $s\mapsto\varphi_Y(s)\in(h_*\mathcal F)(Y)=\mathcal F(X)$. Special cases and names: (a) for $h=\mathrm{id}_Y$ and $\varphi:\mathcal G\to\mathcal F$ a morphism of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules, $\varphi^*=H^p(\varphi)$ is the map induced by the functor $H^p(Y,-)$; (b) the *pullback* $h^*:H^p(Y,\mathcal G)\to H^p(X,h^*\mathcal G)$ is $\varphi^*$ for the unit $\varphi=\eta_{\mathcal G}:\mathcal G\to h_*h^*\mathcal G$; for an open $U\subseteq Y$ and the inclusion $j:U\to Y$ this is the *restriction* $H^p(Y,\mathcal G)\to H^p(U,\mathcal G|_U)$ (with $j^*\mathcal G=\mathcal G|_U$); (c) the *edge map* $e_{h,\mathcal F}:H^p(Y,h_*\mathcal F)\to H^p(X,\mathcal F)$ is $\varphi^*$ for $\varphi=\mathrm{id}_{h_*\mathcal F}$.

source.place: Cohomology of Sheaves, Section 01F7 (section-functoriality): Lemma 01F8 (lemma-functoriality), Equations 01F9/01FA (equation-functorial-derived, equation-functorial) and Remark 01FB (remark-explain-arrow), with Lemma 01EZ (lemma-before-Leray) for the quasi-isomorphism
